newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe manager shoots, wounds 18 striking guards.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe manager shoots, wounds 18 striking guards.

text.p: A Zimbabwean security company manager allegedly shot and wounded 18 guards during a violent demonstration over pay on Thursday, witnesses and police said.
They said the manager opened fire on about 200 guards when they began stoning the company offices in Harare's industrial district.
The striking workers -- demanding a 50 percent wage rise -- later burnt about a dozen company motorbikes before riot police managed to quell the violence.
"We are questioning one manager over the shooting allegations," a police official said, but gave no details.

Zimbabwe has been hit by a wave of short wildcat strikes by workers pressing for hefty pay hikes. Industries that have been affected include banking, textile and clothing, construction, private security services, hotel and catering and rail transport.
Economic analysts say the strikes are undermining Zimbabwe's prospects for sustainable economic growth. The economy is expected rise by six percent this year after an eight percent rise in 1996.

The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) -- which over the weeks has been trying to curtail the strikes through comprehensive negotiations -- accused some employers of playing unreasonably tough, and the government of siding with them.

"The ZCTU notes with regret the current spate of strikes that have gripped the nation...mainly because of the ungrateful bosses who have refused to address the plight of the almost destitute majority workers," it said in a statement on Thursday.
